newsitem.title: USA: Late spot U.S. Midwest seesaws, loses ground.
newsitem.headline: Late spot U.S. Midwest seesaws, loses ground.

text.p: Spot Midwest U.S. propane prices seesawed within an eight-cent range on Thursday, ending the afternoon about four cents down from Wednesday levels, traders said.
Conway propane was sold for as low as 89 cents a gallon and as high as 97 cents, players said, with prices winding up at between 92.0 and 93.0 cents by the end of regular trading hours.
"The market is confused," one trader said, adding that activity was very thin because many players were enjoying holiday parties and at least four hunting outings.
The price-slippage was a "little retracement," the trader said, from the 17-cent-gain in Conway prices since bullish API propane data were released on Monday.

Escalating propane prices spurred two U.S. senators on Thursday to write a letter to Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary, urging her to review the cause of "troubling" price increases and how propane stocks have shrunk to worrisome levels this year.
It was written by Senators Pete Dominici of New Mexico and Frank Murkowski of Alaska, both Republicans from rural states where propane is an important source of heating fuel.
Mont Belvieu propane, meanwhile, was offered at about 68.75 cents, a half cent weaker than Wednesday, traders said.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632
